original_question: Does there exist an integer sequence that is good for 2-recurrence of powers of a single transformation but is not good for 2-recurrence of commuting transformations?
target_in_paper: Section 4.5, Problem 7 (the recurrence problem under “Commuting vs powers of a single transformation”). The draft is aiming at this exact open problem, not at the neighboring convergence question. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right official target: it asks for an existence/nonexistence example, it uses the correct recurrence level (2-recurrence), and it contrasts exactly the two notions the paper contrasts in §4.5: recurrence for powers of one transformation versus recurrence for commuting transformations. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
missing_details: It should explicitly say that the unknown object is a sequence of integers (a(n))_{n∈N}. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

It should unpack “good for 2-recurrence of powers”: for every k1,k2∈Z, every invertible measure-preserving system (X,ℬ,μ,T), and every A∈ℬ with μ(A)>0, there exists n∈N with a(n)≠0 such that μ(A ∩ T^{-k1 a(n)}A ∩ T^{-k2 a(n)}A)>0. A stand-alone question should not leave this buried in the paper’s terminology. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

It should unpack “good for 2-recurrence of commuting transformations”: for every probability space (X,𝓧,μ), every pair of commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations T1,T2:X→X, and every A∈𝓧 with μ(A)>0, there exists n∈N with a(n)≠0 such that μ(A ∩ T1^{-a(n)}A ∩ T2^{-a(n)}A)>0. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

The quantifier over coefficients in the powers case is important: the paper’s notion is not just the special pair (1,2), but all integer coefficients k1,k2. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

To state the negation precisely, the question should say that (a(n)) is not good for 2-recurrence of commuting transformations, meaning that there exist some commuting system and some positive-measure set A for which μ(A ∩ T1^{-a(n)}A ∩ T2^{-a(n)}A)=0 for every n with a(n)≠0. This logical form is implicit in the draft but should be explicit in a stand-alone version. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))

It helps to note that there are no ambient field/ring, degree, homogeneity, or nilpotency hypotheses here; the missing content is entirely in the ergodic-theoretic definitions and quantifiers from §3.1. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))
refined_question: Does there exist a sequence of integers (a(n))_{n∈N} such that for every k1,k2∈Z, every invertible measure-preserving system (X,ℬ,μ,T), and every A∈ℬ with μ(A)>0, there exists n∈N with a(n)≠0 for which μ(A ∩ T^{-k1 a(n)}A ∩ T^{-k2 a(n)}A)>0, but (a(n)) is not good for 2-recurrence of commuting transformations; equivalently, there exist a probability space (X,𝓧,μ), commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations T1,T2:X→X, and A∈𝓧 with μ(A)>0 such that μ(A ∩ T1^{-a(n)}A ∩ T2^{-a(n)}A)=0 for every n∈N with a(n)≠0? ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, does there exist a sequence of integers (a(n)) such that for every k1,k2∈Z and every set E⊂Z of positive upper density, E contains a pattern {m, m+k1 a(n), m+k2 a(n)} for some m∈Z and n∈N with a(n)≠0, but there exist d∈N, vectors v1,v2∈Z^d, and a set F⊂Z^d of positive upper density that contains no pattern {m, m+a(n)v1, m+a(n)v2} with n∈N and a(n)≠0? This is exactly the paper’s combinatorial reformulation of the two recurrence notions. ([users.math.uoc.gr](https://users.math.uoc.gr/~frantzikinakis/OpenProblems/OpenProblems.pdf?utm_source=openai))
justification: The nearest official formulation is exactly the open problem stated in §4.5. Your draft is already very close to the paper’s wording, so the main repair is not to broaden or redirect it, but to make the paper’s terminology explicit. The key hidden content comes from the recurrence definitions in §3.1: the powers notion quantifies over all integer coefficients k1,k2 and one invertible measure-preserving transformation T, while the commuting notion uses two commuting invertible measure-preserving transformations T1,T2 with the same iterate a(n). The paper also gives an explicit combinatorial equivalence in §3.1, so an alternate density formulation is legitimate if desired. ([ar5iv.org](https://ar5iv.org/pdf/1103.3808))
